lessons.title: Measuring Your Available Space in Meters
lessons.body: Before you build or buy anything, you must know exactly how much space you have. Use a tape measure that shows meters and centimeters, not feet. If you only have a foot tape, convert: 1 meter = 3.28 feet. Write down the length and width of the area you plan to use. For a cold room for 4 to 10 beasts, you need a floor area of at least 12 square meters (for 4 beasts) up to 30 square meters (for 10 beasts). A typical beast carcass takes about 1.2 meters by 0.6 meters when hung. So if you hang 10 carcasses side by side with 10 cm gaps, you need a rail length of about 7 meters. But you also need walking space. Measure the height of your ceiling or roof. You need at least 2.4 meters clear height to hang carcasses without them touching the floor. If your space is smaller, you might need a different layout or fewer beasts. Always measure twice. Use a notebook to sketch the dimensions. Mark doors, windows, and any poles or pillars. Check for sloping floors â you will need to level or add drainage. If you are renting, confirm you can modify the space. If building new, ensure the ground is firm and not in a flood path. Remember, hot climates require extra space for air to move. So add 20% to your measured area for ventilation gaps. For example, if you measured 20 square meters, plan for 24 square meters of usable space. Write everything in meters and centimeters. This will save you money and frustration later.

lessons.title: Layout for Easy Loading of Carcasses
lessons.body: The way you arrange your cold room affects how fast you can load and unload carcasses. Speed matters because every minute a carcass is outside, bacteria multiply. Design a straight line from the door to the hanging rail. Do not put the rail behind a wall or around a corner. The door should be wide enough for a wheelbarrow or a hand trolley â at least 1.2 meters wide. Inside, leave a clear aisle of 1 meter between the door and the first hanging position. Hang carcasses perpendicular to the rail so they face the door. This makes it easy to slide them in and out. Use a rail height of 2.2 to 2.4 meters from the floor. If you have 10 beasts, split them into two rows of five, with a 1.5 meter aisle between rows. That way, two people can work at once. For 4 beasts, one row is enough. Install the rail with a slight downward slope toward the door â about 2 cm per meter â so blood and water run out, not into the room. Use stainless steel hooks that slide on the rail. Do not use fixed hooks; they slow you down. Place a table or bench near the door for tools and paperwork. Keep the loading area outside the door clear of obstacles. If you have a vehicle, back it up to within 3 meters of the door. For customers, create a separate small window or door for pickup, so they donât walk through the loading zone. Label the rail positions with numbers or letters. Train your workers to load from the back first, so the oldest carcass is nearest the door. This is called first-in, first-out. A good layout can cut loading time by half.

lessons.title: Positioning for Ventilation in Hot Climates
lessons.body: In hot climates, heat is your enemy. A cold room must get rid of heat from the compressor, from the carcasses, and from the sun. Position your cold room so that the longest wall faces away from the afternoon sun. In Africa, the afternoon sun is in the west. So put the cold room on the east side of a building, or shade the west wall with a tree, a shed, or a shade cloth. Never put the cold room directly under a metal roof without insulation â that roof can reach 60Â°C and radiate heat down. Leave at least 1 meter of open space around the condenser unit (the outside part). If the condenser is boxed in, it cannot release heat. For natural ventilation, place two vents: one low on the cool side (south or east) and one high on the hot side (north or west). The low vent lets in cool morning air; the high vent lets out hot air. Cover vents with mosquito mesh and a rain hood. If you use an evaporative cooler, place it on the shaded side and ensure a cross-breeze. For powered ventilation, install an exhaust fan on the hot side, sized to change the air 10 times per hour. For a 20 cubic meter room, that is 200 cubic meters per hour. Use a fan with a thermostat. Also, keep the door closed as much as possible. Add a plastic strip curtain to the door to block hot air when someone enters. In very hot areas (over 35Â°C), you may need a second fan or a small air conditioner for the compressor room. Test ventilation by hanging a ribbon near the vents â it should move. If it doesnât, adjust. Remember, good ventilation reduces cooling costs by up to 30%.

lessons.title: Floor Drainage for Blood and Water
lessons.body: Blood and water on the floor are dangerous. They make the floor slippery, they breed bacteria, and they can ruin your cold roomâs insulation. You must plan drainage before you pour the floor. The floor should slope toward a drain at a rate of 1 to 2 cm per meter. For a 5 meter wide room, that means the drain is 5 to 10 cm lower than the edges. Use a smooth, non-porous floor material like sealed concrete or epoxy. Do not use tiles with wide grout lines â blood gets stuck there. Install a drain channel (also called a trench drain) across the low end of the room, covered with a stainless steel grate. The channel should be at least 10 cm wide and 10 cm deep, with a slope of 1 cm per meter toward an outside soakaway or sewer. If you cannot put a channel, use a floor drain with a removable strainer to catch solids. The drain pipe must be at least 50 mm (2 inches) in diameter to avoid clogging. Never let blood sit. After each use, flush the floor with water and a disinfectant like bleach (1 part bleach to 10 parts water). For a 10-beast room, you might collect 20 to 30 liters of blood and water per day. So your soakaway must handle that volume. Build a grease trap or a small septic pit outside. If the floor slopes the wrong way, you can add a thin layer of self-leveling concrete, but itâs better to do it right the first time. Also, keep the drain covered when not in use to stop pests. A good drainage system keeps your cold room dry, safe, and smelling clean.

lessons.title: Access for Delivery Vehicles and Customers
lessons.body: Your cold room is only useful if you can get animals in and meat out easily. Plan access for two types of traffic: delivery vehicles (bringing live animals or carcasses) and customers (buying meat). For delivery, you need a driveway that can handle a small truck or a pickup. The driveway should be at least 3 meters wide and have a firm surface â gravel or concrete. If it rains heavily, add a culvert or drainage ditch so the driveway doesnât flood. The delivery door should be at least 1.5 meters wide and 2 meters high, so a truck can back up close. Ideally, the delivery door faces the driveway, and the customer door faces a different direction, like a shop front. That way, customers donât walk through the dirty loading area. For customers, provide a clean, shaded waiting area with a small window or door for ordering. The customer door should be at least 1 meter wide. If you sell directly, have a display fridge or a counter near the customer door. Keep a clear path of 1.2 meters wide from the cold room to the customer area. Parking for customers: at least 2 spaces for cars or motorcycles, each 2.5 meters by 5 meters. If you are in a market, you might not have vehicle access, so plan for hand carts or bicycles. In that case, make sure the path from the cold room to the main road is smooth and at least 1.5 meters wide. Also, consider security: a gate or a guard to control who enters. Label doors clearly: âDeliveryâ and âCustomers.â This separation reduces contamination and speeds up service. Always keep the access routes clear of trash and obstacles.

lessons.title: Sketching Your Cold Room Plan
lessons.body: A sketch is a simple drawing that shows where everything goes. You donât need to be an artist. Use a pencil, a ruler, and graph paper (or a notebook with squares). Each square can represent 0.5 meters. Start by drawing the outline of your room to scale. For example, if your room is 4 meters by 5 meters, draw a rectangle 8 squares by 10 squares. Mark the doors and windows. Show which way the doors open. Next, draw the hanging rail. For 10 beasts, draw a line 7 meters long (14 squares) along one wall, leaving 1 meter from the wall. Mark hook positions every 0.7 meters (about 1.5 squares). Draw the aisle: at least 1 meter wide. Draw the drain channel as a dashed line at the low end. Draw the condenser unit outside the room, at least 1 meter from the wall. Draw the delivery door and the customer door. Add a table near the door. Use arrows to show the path of a carcass from delivery to hanging to customer. Label everything: ârail,â âdrain,â âdoor,â âcondenser,â âaisle.â Write the measurements in meters. If you have a phone, take a photo of your sketch. Show it to a builder or a technician. They can spot mistakes. For example, you might have put the rail too close to the wall, or the drain on the high side. Revise your sketch until it works. Then make a final copy in pen. Keep it in a plastic sleeve. This sketch will guide your construction and help you get quotes. It also helps you plan where to put shelves, knives, and PPE. A good sketch saves money and time.

quiz.q: What is the minimum floor area recommended for a cold room for 4 beasts?
quiz.explanation: For 4 beasts, you need at least 12 square meters to allow for hanging and walking space.

quiz.q: How much clear height do you need to hang carcasses without them touching the floor?
quiz.explanation: A minimum of 2.4 meters clear height prevents carcasses from touching the floor.

quiz.q: Why should you add 20% to your measured area in hot climates?
quiz.explanation: Hot climates require extra space for air movement to help cool the room.

quiz.q: What is the recommended width for a cold room door to allow a wheelbarrow?
quiz.explanation: A door at least 1.2 meters wide allows easy passage for wheelbarrows and trolleys.

quiz.q: How should carcasses be oriented on the rail for easy loading?
options: D) Facing away from the door
quiz.explanation: Perpendicular orientation makes it easy to slide carcasses in and out.

quiz.q: What is the recommended aisle width between two rows of hanging carcasses?
quiz.explanation: A 1.5 meter aisle allows two people to work simultaneously.

quiz.q: Why should the rail slope slightly toward the door?
options: B) To let blood and water run out
quiz.explanation: A slope helps blood and water drain out of the room instead of pooling.

quiz.q: What type of hooks should be used on the rail?
quiz.explanation: Sliding hooks allow quick movement of carcasses along the rail.

quiz.q: In Africa, which direction should the longest wall of the cold room face to avoid afternoon sun?
quiz.explanation: The west wall receives the hot afternoon sun, so it should be avoided or shaded.

quiz.q: How much open space should be left around the condenser unit?
quiz.explanation: At least 1 meter of open space allows the condenser to release heat properly.

quiz.q: Where should the low vent be placed for natural ventilation?
quiz.explanation: The low vent on the cool side lets in cool morning air.

quiz.q: What is the recommended air change rate per hour for a powered exhaust fan?
quiz.explanation: A rate of 10 air changes per hour effectively removes heat from the cold room.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a plastic strip curtain at the door?
options: B) To block hot air when entering
quiz.explanation: Strip curtains create a barrier that reduces hot air entering the cold room.

quiz.q: What is the recommended slope for a cold room floor toward the drain?
quiz.explanation: A slope of 1 to 2 cm per meter allows proper drainage without being too steep.

quiz.q: What floor material is best for a cold room?
quiz.explanation: Sealed concrete or epoxy is smooth, non-porous, and easy to clean.

quiz.q: What is the minimum diameter for a drain pipe to avoid clogging?
quiz.explanation: A 50 mm (2-inch) pipe is large enough to handle blood and water without clogging.

quiz.q: How often should the floor be flushed with disinfectant?
quiz.explanation: Flushing after each use prevents bacteria growth and keeps the room hygienic.

quiz.q: What is a grease trap used for?
options: B) To separate fat from water
quiz.explanation: A grease trap separates fats and oils from wastewater to prevent drain clogs.

quiz.q: How wide should the driveway be for a small delivery truck?
quiz.explanation: A 3-meter wide driveway allows a small truck or pickup to pass easily.

quiz.q: Why should the customer door be separate from the delivery door?
options: B) To avoid contamination and speed service
quiz.explanation: Separate doors keep customers away from the dirty loading area, reducing contamination.

quiz.q: What is the recommended width for a clear path from the cold room to the customer area?
quiz.explanation: A 1.2 meter wide path allows easy movement of people and products.

quiz.q: How many parking spaces should be provided for customers?
quiz.explanation: At least 2 parking spaces (each 2.5 m by 5 m) accommodate cars or motorcycles.

quiz.q: What should you use to draw a cold room plan to scale?
options: A) A ruler and graph paper
quiz.explanation: Graph paper and a ruler help you draw accurate scaled dimensions.

quiz.q: If each square on graph paper represents 0.5 meters, how many squares for a 4-meter wall?
quiz.explanation: 4 meters divided by 0.5 meters per square equals 8 squares.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing between hook positions on the rail?
quiz.explanation: A spacing of 0.7 meters gives enough room for each carcass without crowding.

quiz.q: Why should you show your sketch to a builder or technician?
options: B) To spot mistakes before construction
quiz.explanation: A professional can identify errors like poor drainage or insufficient space.

quiz.q: What does FIFO stand for in loading carcasses?
quiz.explanation: FIFO means the oldest carcass is loaded at the back and removed first from the front.

quiz.q: How can you test if ventilation is working?
options: B) Hang a ribbon near the vents
quiz.explanation: A ribbon moving in the airflow indicates that ventilation is functioning.

quiz.q: What is the recommended bleach solution for disinfecting floors?
options: A) 1 part bleach to 1 part water
B) 1 part bleach to 5 parts water
C) 1 part bleach to 10 parts water
D) 1 part bleach to 20 parts water
quiz.explanation: A 1:10 bleach solution is effective for disinfecting without being too harsh.

quiz.q: Why should you keep the drain covered when not in use?
quiz.explanation: Covering the drain prevents both pests and unpleasant odors from entering the room.
